summary: Parsonsfield, York Co., Maine tower erected 1920 and moved in 1922 to Green Mountain, Effingham NH; no source describes the Maine site today.

facts.design: Steel tower, 48 feet at erection per the 1920 annual report
facts.status_note: Moved in 1922 to Green Mountain, Effingham, New Hampshire; no source describes what remains on Cedar Mountain

staffing.status: Watchman's camp built beside the tower in 1920; joint Maine and New Hampshire upkeep proposed in 1922

visit.trail_note: A Laconia Daily Sun hiking account describes a 1.4-mile trail to the summit tower on Green Mountain, Effingham, New Hampshire.

events.note: Erection of a 48-foot steel tower started in July and was finished in early September
A camp for the watchman was built alongside the tower
Moved to Green Mountain, Effingham NH; the Laconia account gives 1921
Original 47-foot tower shortened to 39 feet (New Hampshire register)
Laconia account says the tower was used until around 1960; approximate date
Registered September 15, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

evidence.supports: Maine began erecting a 48-foot steel tower on Cedar Mountain in Parsonsfield in July 1920
evidence.quote: we started the erection of a forty-eight foot steel tower on Cedar Mountain located in the town of Parsonsfield

evidence.supports: a watchman's camp and a mile of telephone line were built with the tower
evidence.quote: a camp for the accommodation of the watchman, and started building a mile of telephone line on that mountain

evidence.supports: the work was finished in the first week of September 1920
evidence.quote: This work was completed the first week in September.

evidence.supports: in June 1922 plans were reported to move the tower to Green Mountain across the New Hampshire line
evidence.quote: It is now proposed to move the tower to the summit of Green Mountain just across the line in New Hampshire.

evidence.supports: the Daily Kennebec Journal item is dated June 29, 1922
the tower would be taken down
Green Mountain is about 800 feet higher than Cedar Mountain
evidence.quote: Green Mountain is some 800 feet higher than Cedar Mountain.

evidence.supports: the new site has a wider view, reaching the coast
evidence.quote: commands a view clear through to the coast

evidence.supports: the two states were to share the upkeep
evidence.quote: The maintenance of the station will be jointly by the two states

evidence.supports: the Governor and Council approved the plan
evidence.quote: The Governor and Council have given approval to the project.

evidence.supports: the tower was moved to Effingham, New Hampshire in 1922
evidence.quote: The tower was moved to Effingham, New Hampshire in 1922.

evidence.supports: the register says the Green Mountain lookout was moved from Cedar Mountain in 1922
evidence.quote: Green Mountain lookout was moved from Cedar Mountain, ME in 1922.

evidence.supports: the Laconia account dates the move to 1921
evidence.quote: In 1921, the fire tower was moved from Cedar Mountain, Maine, to its current location.

evidence.supports: the Laconia hiker drove to Effingham, New Hampshire, to climb to the Green Mountain summit tower
evidence.quote: we drove first to Effingham via Routes 25 east to 153 south

evidence.supports: the New Hampshire tower was used until around 1960
evidence.quote: was used continuously until around 1960 when fire towers became obsolete

evidence.supports: the original 47-foot tower was cut to 39 feet in 1977
evidence.quote: The original 47' steel tower was shortened to 39' in 1977

evidence.supports: the tower is now in part-time service
the Laconia account gives the tower a height of 60 feet
evidence.quote: Upon reaching the summit, I was struck by the 60-foot fire tower that rose before me.

evidence.supports: a 1.4-mile trail leads to the summit
evidence.quote: started up the 1.4-mile trail to the summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Fire Lookout Association and the New Hampshire register both give 1922; a Laconia Daily Sun hiking account gives 1921. The record uses 1922 because two sources agree on it, and the story notes the difference.

sources.title: Green Mountain and Ossipee Pine Barrens: Nature's Diversity in Southeast Carroll County

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' confirmed: the structure moved to Green Mountain, Effingham NH. Heights conflict and are not resolved, so height_m is not set: 48 feet in the 1920 report, 47 feet original and 39 feet after 1977 in the NH register, 60 feet in the Laconia account. No access level set: the Maine site is not described, and NH climbing rules were not found. An AllTrails page on the summit deck returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Facebook posts (tower up 1919-1921; move 1922) were not used. Two WebSearch calls and about ten page reads, over the read budget because the moved structure needed New Hampshire sources.
